claims.text: High-entropy alloys with a predominantly FCC structure will exhibit enhanced ductility.
Activation of multiple slip systems in an FCC structure enhances ductility.
The multicomponent alloy can be tuned to exhibit a predominantly FCC phase.
Optimized heat treatment can promote formation of a homogeneous FCC microstructure.
Precise compositional tuning can promote formation of a homogeneous FCC microstructure.
The intervention will produce a predominant and uniformly distributed FCC phase.
The intervention will produce refined grain boundaries.
Multiple slip systems are inherent in the FCC structure.
Grain-boundary sliding supplements slip-mediated ductility in a nanostructured regime.
The treated alloy will have a statistically significant increase in percent elongation relative to the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will have a statistically significant increase in strain to failure relative to the untreated baseline.
The untreated baseline alloy has mixed phases and lacks targeted phase-homogenization or grain-boundary treatment.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis defines the outcome in terms of statistical significance, while the falsification rule also equates failure with less than 20% improvement. Statistical significance and a 20% effect-size threshold are not equivalent, so a statistically significant improvement below 20%, or a non-significant improvement above 20%, would yield conflicting decisions.
